+import numpy as np

+

+

+
+print("Test 1: multiply no mask by constant")
+res = nref_nomask.multiply(1., handle_mask=np.bitwise_or)
+print("mask:", res.mask)

+
+print("\nTest 2: multiply no mask by itself")

+

+import pandas as pd
+import numpy as np
+from seaborn._stats.regression import PolyFit
+
+print("Testing PolyFit edge cases...")
+
+# Test 1: Missing values in x and y
+print("\n1. Testing with None in x and y...")
+data1 = pd.DataFrame({"x": [1, 2, 3, None, 4], "y": [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]})
+stat = PolyFit(order=2, gridsize=10)
+result1 = stat._fit_predict(data1)
+print(f"Result length: {len(result1)}, expected: 10")
+assert len(result1) == 10, "Failed with None in x"
+print("PASSED")
+
+# Test 2: All NaN values
+print("\n2. Testing with all NaN values...")
+data2 = pd.DataFrame({"x": [None, None], "y": [None, None]})
+result2 = stat._fit_predict(data2)
+print(f"Result length: {len(result2)}, expected: 0")
+assert len(result2) == 0, "Failed with all NaN"
+print("PASSED")
+
+# Test 3: Missing values only in y
+print("\n3. Testing with NaN in y only...")
+data3 = pd.DataFrame({"x": [1, 2, 3, 4], "y": [1, None, 3, 4]})
+result3 = stat._fit_predict(data3)
+print(f"Result length: {len(result3)}, expected: 10")
+assert len(result3) == 10, "Failed with NaN in y"
+print("PASSED")
+
+# Test 4: Missing values only in x
+print("\n4. Testing with NaN in x only...")
+data4 = pd.DataFrame({"x": [1, None, 3, 4], "y": [1, 2, 3, 4]})
+result4 = stat._fit_predict(data4)
+print(f"Result length: {len(result4)}, expected: 10")
+assert len(result4) == 10, "Failed with NaN in x"
+print("PASSED")
+

+
